clue.text: Stop evil AI getting back to planet

indicators.note: the back of a word is its tail end, so only the final letter of the following word is kept

blocks.note: HAL 9000 is the murderous computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey
the final letter of planet

explanation.surface: A plea to halt a rogue artificial intelligence before it gets back to the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is to stop, as a verb meaning bring or come to a standstill.

clue.text: Completely lost, having ruined atlas with ale

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper form, so the letters of these words are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller who spilt beer over the map has no idea where they are.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being bewildered or confused borrows the image of a ship out of sight of land.

clue.text: A certain McCartney reported to do with the stars

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word heard rather than written

blocks.note: the adjective for anything relating to the heavenly bodies; in a non-rhotic British accent its final R is silent

explanation.surface: Something about a McCartney being linked to celebrity, as reported in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Stella McCartney, the fashion designer and daughter of Paul, is the McCartney meant. The homophone relies on British speech dropping the final R.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is the first name of the designer daughter of Beatle Paul McCartney, one particular member of that family.

clue.text: Saint given a day? Figures

blocks.note: ST is the standard abbreviation for saint
taken as written
TUES is the abbreviation for Tuesday

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a saint gets a feast day of their own, then a muttered verdict on the numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures here are sculpted representations of people, which is what statues are.

clue.text: Relative of husky bloke unable to speak

blocks.note: a bloke is a man
mute means silent or unable to talk

explanation.surface: A man with a hoarse, husky voice has lost it completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' reads as an adjective for a gravelly voice beside 'bloke', but it is the sled dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The malamute is an Alaskan sled dog breed closely related to the Siberian husky.

clue.text: Prickly plant beginning to tickle one under canvas

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of tickle
an artist's canvas rests on an easel, so the stand is the thing beneath it

explanation.surface: A spiky plant pokes a camper sleeping in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under canvas' usually means camping in a tent; here it is a painter's canvas sitting on its stand.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a tall thistle-like plant with spiny flower heads once used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Crossword setter copied and pasted some online content

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me
a copy of the previous piece, so it appears twice

explanation.surface: A setter caught plagiarising material found on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: Copying and pasting the setter duplicates the same two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is a humorous image or idea spread and shared widely on the internet.

clue.text: Transport lobby called out

indicators.note: words called out are spoken, so the sound of the word is what counts

blocks.note: a lobby is an entrance hall

explanation.surface: A transport lobby group being summoned or denounced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport lobby' looks like a pressure group; 'Transport' is a verb and the lobby is a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul goods is to carry or drag them from one place to another, a synonym of transport as a verb.

clue.text: One attached to bottle's taken in by fancy settee for confidential chats

indicators.note: to be taken in by something is to be absorbed inside it, so one piece sits within the other
fancy means elaborate or imaginative, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange
the rubber nipple fitted to a baby's feeding bottle

explanation.surface: A baby's bottle has been swallowed up by an ornate sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: The bottle is a baby's feeding bottle, and the settee only supplies letters; the chats take their name from French for head to head.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private conversation between two people, typically intimate and confidential.

clue.text: Parts regularly given to a stalwart old spear-carrier

indicators.note: taking parts at regular intervals means keeping every other letter of the words concerned

blocks.note: taken as written
the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Bit-part roles handed out regularly to a faithful veteran actor who carries a spear on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'spear-carrier' is theatre slang for an extra, which suits the surface; here it is literal, a device for launching spears.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlatl is an ancient spear-thrower, a notched stick that holds the shaft and adds leverage when it is hurled.

clue.text: Getting a point for runs, wipes floor with competition

indicators.note: getting something in exchange signals a swap of one letter in the word
one thing given for another is put in its place, so a letter is replaced

blocks.note: to wipe the floor with someone is to beat them soundly
E for east, a point of the compass
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket side scoring heavily and crushing its rivals in a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The R in THRASHES is swapped for E. The Ashes is the Test cricket series played between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is a long-running cricket contest between England and Australia, so it is a named sporting contest.

clue.text: Ship meals primarily consumed with this person?

definitions.text: Ship meals primarily consumed with this person?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept

blocks.note: the setter speaking of themself
SS, steamship, prefixes ship names
the opening letter of meals
consumed food, so ate

explanation.surface: A question about who on board you share your meals with.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: on a ship the crew eat together in the mess, and the companion you eat with there is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A messmate is a sailor who eats in the same mess, the shipboard dining group, as another.

clue.text: Cheer's echo not appearing after expected interval

blocks.note: Echo is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for E
something late has not turned up when it was due

explanation.surface: A shout of applause whose echo never comes back when it should.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to fill someone with joy, as a verb synonym for cheer up or delight.

clue.text: A couple of extra marks possibly given to us in German class

definitions.text: A couple of extra marks possibly given to us in German class

blocks.clueFragment: A couple of extra marks possibly given to us in German class
blocks.note: surface reading: a teacher generously awarding pupils a bonus point or two

blocks.clueFragment: A couple of extra marks possibly given to us
blocks.note: setter's reading: two dots that may be placed over the letter U in German

explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' is read as the plural of the letter U, and 'marks' are written diacritics rather than grades.
explanation.definitionFit: An umlaut is the pair of dots written over a vowel in German, as in über, to show a changed sound.

clue.text: Group of theologians involved in rulemaking

indicators.note: something involved in a word is wrapped up inside it, so the letters run on within it

blocks.note: the second to sixth letters

explanation.surface: Religious scholars taking part in drafting laws.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulema are the body of Muslim scholars trained in Islamic law and theology.

clue.text: Celebrated Indian bowler possibly embraced by mother

indicators.note: something embraced is held in arms, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: an informal word for mother
a bowler is a kind of hat; 'possibly' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A famous Indian cricketer, perhaps a bowler, being hugged by his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' sounds like cricket next to 'Indian', but it is the round felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma, meaning great soul, is an honorific given to revered figures, most famously Gandhi.

clue.text: Those inspiring works capturing tastes now and then

indicators.note: only occasionally, so just every other letter of the word is kept
to capture is to take something in and hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the Muses were the Greek goddesses who inspired the arts
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Inspirational creations that occasionally capture changing fashions.
explanation.definitionFit: Must-sees are films, shows or artworks so highly regarded that nobody should miss them.

clue.text: Dodgy salesmen ignoring latest viral complaint

indicators.note: ignoring the latest part means leaving off the final letter
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shady sales reps paying no attention to the newest internet sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viral' suggests online trends with dodgy salesmen; it is literal here, an illness caused by a virus.
explanation.definitionFit: Measles is an infectious disease caused by a virus, so it is an illness of viral origin.

clue.text: Endeavour and others latch onto leads from the least expected sources

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters, so the first of each is kept

blocks.note: to latch a door is to shut it
the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Endeavour and its colleagues seizing on clues from the most unlikely informants.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour suggests the TV detective Morse, whose first name it is; here it is the NASA orbiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Endeavour was one of NASA's space shuttles, alongside Atlantis, Discovery and others.

clue.text: Two large countries turning on Luxembourg in predictable way

indicators.note: turning round makes the letters run the opposite direction

blocks.note: AUS for Australia and USA for the United States
L is Luxembourg's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: Two big nations rounding on tiny Luxembourg, as one might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the turned countries sit over the L.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase as usual describes something happening in the normal, expected manner.

clue.text: Hires reins after horse has bolted

indicators.note: after something has gone, what remains is the rest of the word without it
something that has bolted has run off, so it is no longer in the word

blocks.note: leashes are straps that restrain, like reins
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Someone renting out tack once the horse has already escaped, too late.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes shutting the stable door after the horse has bolted. Horse and H are both slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease property is to hire it for rent, so leases and hires work as present-tense verbs.

clue.text: Methuselah repeatedly shelled out for professional solver

indicators.note: shelling strips the outer casing, and doing it twice removes two layers of end letters
out here means disordered or wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written; it is also this setter's pseudonym

explanation.surface: The setter Methuselah paying out over and over to a professional crossword solver.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the outer pair twice leaves THUSEL, which is then rearranged. 'Solver' suggests crosswords; it means a solver of crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, someone whose job is to solve mysteries and crimes.

clue.text: Completed maths problems involving area for things with segments

indicators.note: to involve something is to include it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to sit an exam is to complete it, so sat
sums are arithmetic exercises
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A pupil has finished their maths homework involving area calculations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Segments' suggests geometry beside maths problems; here it means the sections of a citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Satsumas are small easy-peel mandarin oranges whose flesh divides into segments.

clue.text: Selection of items arranged by caddy, might you say?

indicators.note: what you might say is what is spoken, so the sound rather than the spelling counts

blocks.note: a golf caddy might set up a golf ball peg, so a peg is set

explanation.surface: A set of things neatly laid out beside a tea caddy.
explanation.walkthrough: The caddy reads as a tea caddy, which fits the answer; the wordplay uses a golf caddy setting a tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea set is a matching collection of cups, saucers, teapot and jug, a set of crockery.

clue.text: Checks out female beasts of burden?

blocks.note: first meaning: evaluates or examines
second meaning: a whimsical coinage, she-asses, like lioness or tigress

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second sense is invented: the -ess ending that makes female nouns added to ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or appraise, so assesses works as a present-tense verb for examines.

clue.text: Old sailor that barnacle clings to?

blocks.note: first meaning: an experienced seaman
second meaning: barnacles live attached to rocks and hulls in sea water

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose second sense: a barnacle clinging to a ship's hull is surrounded by the brine of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt, short for old salt, is slang for a veteran mariner, and it also stands for the seawater barnacles inhabit.

clue.text: Confirm where fans of 11 may be found

definitions.text: where fans of 11 may be found

blocks.note: first meaning: to bear witness to or vouch for

blocks.clueFragment: where fans of 11 may be found
blocks.note: second meaning: Ashes supporters gather at a Test match, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to the answer at 11-across, the cricket series made up of Test matches, so its supporters are 'at Test'.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare something true or certify it, a verb synonym for confirm.

clue.text: Stomach's turned by lewd material

indicators.note: something turned is put the other way round, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: tum is an informal word for stomach, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Someone feeling queasy when confronted with obscene material.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is indecent or obscene writing or pictures, so lewd material in noun form.

clue.text: Suspect tame as hell in spite of everything

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious or not right, so the letters need rearranging

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something dull and mild, yet suspicious nonetheless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase all the same means nevertheless or regardless, conceding a point but carrying on.

clue.text: Flightless birds in muddle not using wings

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two flanks, so the outer letters are dropped

blocks.note: to bemuse is to confuse or muddle

explanation.surface: Birds that cannot fly getting into a confused state without the use of their wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muddle' looks like a noun after 'in'; it is a verb meaning confuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large Australian ratites that cannot fly, second in size only to the ostrich.
